claims.text: Moderate thermal exposure of a metastable Mg-containing lightweight HEA induces a diffusion-driven transformation.
During this transformation, Mg segregates and precipitates as Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates form preferentially at grain boundaries as well as within the matrix.
Precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallics locally depletes the surrounding matrix of Mg.
Local Mg depletion changes the chemistry of surface and subsurface oxide formation.
Elemental depletion associated with oxide formation can accompany non-protective oxidation behavior in an HEA.
Coarse or heterogeneous intermetallic precipitation reduces the integrity or adherence of the protective oxide layer.
Loss of oxide-layer integrity degrades both corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the initial metastable state.
A reported Mg-containing lightweight HEA exhibited complex precipitates in its as-cast structure.
The initial as-cast baseline has a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure.
Aging at approximately 400°C for increasing durations will produce a measurable increase in Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
The transformed material will exhibit a less uniform and less protective oxide scale than the initial state.
The transformed material will show lower electrochemical impedance and higher corrosion current in 3.5 wt.% NaCl than the initial state.
The transformed material will show faster oxidation weight gain or greater oxide-scale spallation than the initial state.
The proposed transformation is relevant primarily in a moderate-temperature service window of about 300–500°C.
At very low temperatures or in extremely aggressive environments, the kinetics or consequences of the transformation may differ.
XRD and SEM/EDS can be used to test for the predicted precipitates and associated compositional partitioning.
The precipitation kinetics, time to critical Mg depletion, quantitative oxide-scale effects, and influence of other alloying elements remain unresolved.
